patch.value: GH-784: SDK blueprint preflight misses host-owned flag collisions and malformed long-flag tokens

Align author-time extension lint and preflight with loader enforcement. lintExtensionBlueprint and assertExtensionPreflight currently return clean reports for a blueprint whose --json declaration is rejected at activation, and neither validator rejects malformed long tokens such as verbose or -v. Add one shared host-owned flag collision rule and explicit long-token grammar so static preflight cannot approve a blueprint the runtime quarantines.

lintExtensionBlueprint emits an error-severity host-owned flag collision finding for primary and alias tokens in SUBCOMMAND_GLOBAL_FLAG_CONTRACTS; assertExtensionPreflight surfaces the same failure and remediation as runtime activation; FlagDefinition.long rejects tokens outside the canonical double-dash grammar at author-time and activation boundaries; valid custom flags remain accepted; SDK types docs fixtures property tests and installed-extension acceptance tests stay aligned
Published @unbrained/pm-cli 2026.7.28 in a clean installed consumer
Lint and preflight an extension blueprint declaring --json, verbose, or -v as FlagDefinition.long, then compare activation behavior.
Static preflight rejects every loader-invalid host-owned or malformed long flag with the same actionable remediation.
Static lint/preflight report no findings for --json while activation rejects it, and malformed long tokens are accepted and stored verbatim.
Extension authors can publish a blueprint after the purpose-built preflight reports success, then lose the affected command or extension surface only at activation.
